screening_threshold.scope: sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold: one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, screened and not a bound on either
screening_threshold.role: decision threshold: an effect smaller than this bound is not distinguishable from repeat-plus-drift

timestamps.name: uniform-grid phase error at the top of the analysed band
timestamps.criterion: worst-case phase error of the uniform grid at the top of the analysed band: max_k |t_k - (t_0 + k x uniform_period_s)| x f_max <= 1/16 cycle, one criterion per input, f_max the Nyquist limit of that input's own profile rate
timestamps.justification: a sample the uniform grid places dt away from its recorded time is mis-phased by 2 pi f dt for every resolved component at f, so max|t_k - grid| x f_max is the worst-case phase error over the analysed band; 1/16 of a cycle (pi/8 rad) keeps the worst-placed sample's coherent (zero-lag) weight at cos(pi/8) = 0.924 of its unbiased value, i.e. caps the amplitude bias of the coherent sums and of the PSD cross terms at 7.6%, and keeps every sample inside its own cycle of the fastest resolved component so none can be attributed to a neighbouring cycle. The tolerance is a grid-error tolerance and says nothing about the flow; the four published statistics describe the recorded intervals themselves, while max_grid_residual_s also carries their cumulative departure, which is what a quantized interval accumulates over a record
timestamps.estimator: uniform grid at each record's own mean inter-profile interval, the period its first and last recorded timestamps imply; the residual is measured against that grid, not against a nominal PRF period
timestamps.decision: uniform grid retained: every input's worst-case phase error is below the tolerance at the top of the band it is analysed in, so the recorded timestamps need no resampling and no irregular-time estimator

time.rule: largest integer number of nominal revolutions fitting every PRF recording, truncated per file by the recorded timestamps

depth.native_grid: each level keeps its own decoded gate grid for the distributional metrics, the gradient and the correlation length; nothing is resampled

grid.acf_estimator: biased (divide-by-N) autocovariance of the mean-removed segment

temporal.mixer_setpoint_role: nominal mixer marker only (500 RPM -> 8.33 Hz, one revolution = 0.12 s): no tachometer in these files, so the setpoint is not a phase reference and no spectral peak or harmonic is attributed to it

floor.role: sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold: one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, screened and not a bound on either (temporal)

alignment.knot_rule: the longer-period level's native gate depths inside the common support, so the knot spacing is never finer than that participant's own grid; the shorter-period level is sampled at each knot by its nearest native gate, never interpolated

definitions.prf_period_us: decoded pulse-repetition period in microseconds, re-checked against the manifest cell: the ladder's key, ordered by it, never by a filename
definitions.velo_max_mm_s: the reader's +/-Nyquist velocity, the velocity at full-scale count (ChannelConfig.velo_max_ms), re-checked against the manifest cell: the unambiguous limit every load fraction is normalised by
definitions.velocity_scale: the +/-Nyquist velocity is the velocity at full-scale count, so a pure PRF change must move it in inverse proportion; velo_max_ms x prf_period_us is audited for constancy and a ladder whose scale moved with anything else is refused
definitions.profile_rate_hz: 1 / (duration_s / (profiles - 1)) from the recorded timestamps: the actual profile rate of that file, not the PRF and not a stored setting
definitions.load_over_velo_max: |v| / velo_max_ms of one sample: 1.0 is the unambiguous limit
definitions.warning_fractions: share of windowed, supported samples at or above 0.5, 0.75, 0.9 and 1.0 of that recording's velo_max_ms; the inner three are declared margins below the limit, not instrument flags, and these files carry no warning channel
definitions.wrap_like_discontinuity: a consecutive-profile change at one gate of at least velo_max_ms with a sign reversal: a wrap moves the estimate across the whole +/-velo_max_ms span in one profile interval, about 2 x velo_max_ms, so the criterion is the conservative half-span
definitions.difference: signed faster - slower per-gate time mean at every common knot, mm/s; a negative value means the shorter period is slower there
definitions.screening_threshold: the committed sole-pair observed-discrepancy screening threshold max_gate_abs_mean_difference_mm_s, read from reference-repeat.provenance.json and pinned to this manifest's hash: the threshold every mean-profile effect is screened against. An effect above or below it is a screening outcome, not proof of a PRF effect and not a bound on repeatability or uncontrolled drift
definitions.matched_segment: the physical segment duration every file is analysed in, the largest multiple of 0.1 s that fits five whole segments in the shortest record; each file takes the whole number of profiles inside it, so segment duration and resolution agree rather than being equal
definitions.comparison_bands: identical bands from the nominal resolution up to the narrowest usable bandwidth in the ladder; a level's density is its band power over the band width, the power being the trapezoidal integral of its own PSD over the frequency bins that band holds, so spectra are compared only where every recording has support
definitions.usable_bandwidth: the highest frequency a file's matched segment supports, half its profile rate; the full-record Nyquist limit is published beside it
definitions.acf_e_folding_lag: the first lag of the mean-removed segment's normalized autocovariance below 1/e, in seconds on that file's own lag grid
definitions.mixer_marker: nominal 500 RPM -> 8.33 Hz marker only: no tachometer in these files, so it is not a phase reference and no peak here is attributed to it or to a harmonic
definitions.replicates: no profile and no gate is an independent experimental replicate
definitions.views: distributional metrics use the common-duration window on the common support; native-grid gradients and correlation lengths use each level's own grid; the full record is analysed only through the matched temporal view

effect_gate.statement: Effect gate: over the 10 pairs the largest absolute per-knot mean difference is 37.51 mm/s (400 vs 500 us at 13.86 mm; depth ranges above the screening_threshold 10.1627..10.1627; 13.8627..15.7127; 34.2127..39.7627) = 1.94 of the WP1 screening_threshold 19.37 mm/s, and 8 pairs clear it somewhere.

velocity_headroom.statement: Velocity headroom: at the plan's 400 us setting the largest |v| in the common window and support is 0.7266 of the 231.2 mm/s unambiguous limit, with 0 sample(s) beyond it and 0 wrap-like discontinuity(ies); the largest load anywhere in the ladder is 1.211 at 800 us, so the pressure on the velocity scale grows as the period lengthens, not as it shortens.

temporal_bandwidth.statement: Temporal bandwidth: the actual profile rate falls from 66.72 Hz to 33.57 Hz across the ladder and the usable bandwidth with it (33.36 to 16.47 Hz), so the shorter period carries the wider band. Spectra are compared only inside 0.625-16.25 Hz, the bands every recording supports, at a nominal resolution of 0.625 Hz. The 8.333 Hz mixer marker sits inside that band for all five levels (0.83 of the 400 us level's in-band power is below it) and stays a marker: no peak is attributed to it or to a harmonic, whose second multiple (16.67 Hz) is above the shared band.

focus_decision.statement: Plan decision, 400 vs 250 us: at 400 us the window's peak load is 0.7266 of a 231.2 mm/s limit (0 sample(s) beyond it, 0 wrap-like step(s)) with the widest usable bandwidth in the ladder (33.36 Hz of 33.36-16.47 Hz), while a 250 us setting would raise the limit to 369.9 mm/s, which nothing here needs. Verdict: this evidence does not show the 400 us setting to be inadequate on either count, so it does not justify a 250 us acquisition. Unidentifiable here: a wrap that leaves no step of half the span (a slowly drifting alias), the peak velocity of a flow whose setpoint differs from this 500-RPM one, and the rate a future 250 us setting would run at, which these files cannot fix because their own rate is not an exact multiple of the PRF. What would overturn it: a recording whose |v| reaches the 400 us unambiguous limit, or a stated question needing temporal content above the 400 us bandwidth.

limitations: The screening threshold is the only repeat, 19.37 mm/s per gate (max_gate_abs_mean_difference_mm_s): one observed realization of repeatability plus uncontrolled drift, not a bound on either. The levels are separate recordings with no acquisition order, so a smaller effect cannot be separated from drift and a larger one could still be drift or one recording rather than the PRF. No level is replicated.

The velocity scale is the key's own consequence (Vmax x prf_period is constant across the ladder to the audited tolerance), but the profile rate is not: it rises from 33.57 to 66.72 Hz while its ratio to the PRF period varies by 0.00625 relative, so the rate is a separate measured property and nothing here claims a future setting would scale it.

The temporal metrics are screened against the same-settings WP1 pair through its committed curves (prf/600.BDD vs res/1-8.BDD), resummarised in 0.625-16.25 Hz on the bands this ladder shares; one pair cannot estimate that floor's own spread, and 5-10 segments per level make a band level a coarse magnitude.

The files carry the velocity-time index only: the 500-RPM setpoint is a marker rather than a phase reference, the spectra are per gate, and a wrap-like step is counted as a discontinuity of the recorded estimate, never as proof that a particular sample aliased. This module owns the PRF axis only: resolution, burst, TGC, emitting power and emissions per profile are neither analysed nor decided here.
